import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.74

by J. G. Thompson

Is the intersection of two good subnormal subgroups of an arbitrary group again good?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.74»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is subnormal if there is a finite chain
$H = H_0 \trianglelefteq H_1 \trianglelefteq \cdots \trianglelefteq H_n = G$.
For subgroups $A$ and $B$ of $G$, the conditions $A \le B$ and
$B \le N_G(A)$ say that $A$ is normal in $B$. -/
def IsSubnormal (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen (fun A B : Subgroup G ↦ A ≤ B ∧ B ≤ A.normalizer) H ⊤

/-- A subnormal subgroup $H$ of $G$ is good if the subgroup generated by $H$ and
any subnormal subgroup $J$ is subnormal in $G$. -/
def IsGood (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  IsSubnormal H ∧ ∀ J : Subgroup G, IsSubnormal J → IsSubnormal (H ⊔ J)

/--
Is it true that whenever $H$ and $K$ are good subnormal subgroups of an arbitrary
(possibly infinite) group $G$, their intersection $H \cap K$ is good?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.74» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type*) [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G),
      IsGood H → IsGood K → IsGood (H ⊓ K) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.74»
modeling_decisions: Modeled a finite subnormal chain as `Relation.ReflTransGen` from `H` to `⊤` of the relation `A ≤ B ∧ B ≤ A.normalizer`. The normalizer characterization says exactly that `A` is normal in `B`.
Defined goodness to include that `H` is subnormal, together with the requirement that `H ⊔ J` is subnormal for every subnormal `J`.
Used subgroup join `⊔` for the generated subgroup `⟨H, J⟩` and subgroup infimum `⊓` for intersection. No finiteness assumption is imposed on the group.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.74

by J. G. Thompson

A subnormal subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is called good if the join
$H \sqcup J$ is subnormal in $G$ for every subnormal subgroup $J$ of $G$.
Is the intersection of two good subnormal subgroups always good?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.74»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is subnormal if there is a finite chain
$H = H_0 \triangleleft H_1 \triangleleft \cdots \triangleleft H_n = G$.
The conditions `Hᵢ ≤ Hᵢ₊₁` and `Hᵢ₊₁ ≤ Hᵢ.normalizer` say that $H_i$ is
normal in $H_{i+1}$. -/
def IsSubnormal (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∃ chain : ℕ → Subgroup G,
    chain 0 = H ∧ chain n = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ i : ℕ, i < n →
        chain i ≤ chain (i + 1) ∧ chain (i + 1) ≤ (chain i).normalizer

/-- A subnormal subgroup $H$ of $G$ is good if $H \sqcup J$ is subnormal in
$G$ whenever $J$ is a subnormal subgroup of $G$. -/
def IsGood (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  IsSubnormal H ∧ ∀ J : Subgroup G, IsSubnormal J → IsSubnormal (H ⊔ J)

/--
Is it true that when $H$ and $K$ are good subnormal subgroups of an arbitrary
(possibly infinite) group $G$, their intersection $H \cap K$ is good?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.74» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type*) [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G),
      IsGood H → IsGood K → IsGood (H ⊓ K) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.74»
modeling_decisions: Subnormality is represented by a natural-number-indexed finite chain with endpoints H and ⊤; only the steps before the endpoint are constrained.
A step Hᵢ ◁ Hᵢ₊₁ is encoded as Hᵢ ≤ Hᵢ₊₁ together with Hᵢ₊₁ ≤ Hᵢ.normalizer, which Mathlib identifies with normality of Hᵢ as a subgroup of Hᵢ₊₁.
The source's term “good” includes the requirement that H itself is subnormal, as well as the join condition for every subnormal J.
The theorem ranges over arbitrary group types and imposes no finiteness assumption; subgroup generation and intersection are represented by lattice join and meet.

by J. G. Thompson

A subnormal subgroup $H \mathrel{\lhd\!\lhd} G$ is called good if
$\langle H, J \rangle \mathrel{\lhd\!\lhd} G$ for every subnormal subgroup

namespace Kourovka.«8.74»

universe u

variable {G : Type u} [Group G]

/-- A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is subnormal if there is a finite chain
$H = H_0 \mathrel{\lhd} H_1 \mathrel{\lhd} \cdots
\mathrel{\lhd} H_n = G$. -/
def IsSubnormal (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (chain : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G),
    chain 0 = H ∧ chain (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ i : Fin n,
        chain i.castSucc ≤ chain i.succ ∧
          ((chain i.castSucc).subgroupOf (chain i.succ)).Normal

/-- A subnormal subgroup $H$ of $G$ is good if $H \sqcup J$ is subnormal in
$G$ whenever $J$ is subnormal in $G$. -/

  IsSubnormal H ∧ ∀ J : Subgroup G, IsSubnormal J → IsSubnormal (H ⊔ J)

Is it true that if $H$ and $K$ are good subnormal subgroups of an arbitrary
group $G$, then $H \cap K$ is good?
-/

  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.74»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.74

by J. G. Thompson

A subnormal subgroup $H \lhd\lhd G$ of a group $G$ is said to be *good* if and only if
$\langle H, J \rangle \lhd\lhd G$ whenever $J \lhd\lhd G$. Is it true that when $H$ and $K$
are good subnormal subgroups of $G$, then $H \cap K$ is good?

Here $H \lhd\lhd G$ means that $H$ is a subnormal subgroup of $G$, i.e. there is a finite chain
of subgroups $H = H_0 \lhd H_1 \lhd \dots \lhd H_n = G$, each normal in the next. The group $G$
is arbitrary (in a finite group the join of two subnormal subgroups is always subnormal, by a
theorem of Wielandt, so every subnormal subgroup of a finite group is good).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.74»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/--
A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is *subnormal*, written $H \lhd\lhd G$, if there is a finite chain
of subgroups $H = H_0 \lhd H_1 \lhd \dots \lhd H_n = G$ in which each $H_i$ is a normal subgroup
of $H_{i+1}$. Here "$A$ is a normal subgroup of $B$" is expressed as `A ≤ B` together with
`(A.subgroupOf B).Normal`.
-/
def IsSubnormal (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen (fun A B : Subgroup G => A ≤ B ∧ (A.subgroupOf B).Normal) H ⊤

/--
A subnormal subgroup $H \lhd\lhd G$ of a group $G$ is *good* if $\langle H, J \rangle \lhd\lhd G$
whenever $J \lhd\lhd G$. The subgroup generated by $H$ and $J$ is the join `H ⊔ J`.
-/
def IsGood (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  IsSubnormal H ∧ ∀ J : Subgroup G, IsSubnormal J → IsSubnormal (H ⊔ J)

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isSubnormal_top : IsSubnormal (⊤ : Subgroup G) :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen.refl

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isSubnormal_of_normal {H : Subgroup G} (hH : H.Normal) : IsSubnormal H :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen.single ⟨le_top, hH.subgroupOf ⊤⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsGood.isSubnormal {H : Subgroup G} (hH : IsGood H) : IsSubnormal H :=
  hH.1

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isGood_top : IsGood (⊤ : Subgroup G) :=
  ⟨isSubnormal_top, fun J _ => by simpa [top_sup_eq] using isSubnormal_top⟩

/--
A subnormal subgroup $H \lhd\lhd G$ of a group $G$ is said to be *good* if and only if
$\langle H, J \rangle \lhd\lhd G$ whenever $J \lhd\lhd G$. Is it true that when $H$ and $K$
are good subnormal subgroups of $G$, then $H \cap K$ is good?

The question is asked for all groups $G$. The intersection $H \cap K$ is the meet `H ⊓ K`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.74» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G),
      IsGood H → IsGood K → IsGood (H ⊓ K) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.74»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition is correct: the statement is one yes/no question over all groups, with 'subnormal' and 'good' as auxiliary definitions.
modeling_decisions: Subnormality is encoded with `Relation.ReflTransGen` of the relation `A ≤ B ∧ (A.subgroupOf B).Normal` from `H` to `⊤`; the reflexive case gives `H = G` (chain of length 0), matching the usual convention that G is subnormal in itself. The explicit `A ≤ B` is essential: without it `(A.subgroupOf B).Normal` only says A ⊓ B is normal in B and every subgroup would become 'subnormal' through B = ⊥.

`IsGood H` includes the subnormality of H as a conjunct (as in the source: 'a subnormal subgroup H is said to be good if …'). Hence the conclusion `IsGood (H ⊓ K)` also asserts subnormality of H ⊓ K, which is automatically true (intersections of subnormal subgroups are subnormal), so the mathematical content is exactly the join condition, as the decomposition notes require.
`⟨H, J⟩` is formalized as the lattice join `H ⊔ J` of subgroups (= closure of the union) and `H ∩ K` as the meet `H ⊓ K`.

The group is quantified as `(G : Type) [Group G]` (universe 0), following the convention of the existing Kourovka files (1_40, 19_25); no finiteness assumption is imposed, since the source asks about arbitrary groups and the question is trivial for finite groups by Wielandt's theorem.

Four short `@[category API]` lemmas (`isSubnormal_top`, `isSubnormal_of_normal`, `IsGood.isSubnormal`, `isGood_top`) were added as basic API tests for the bespoke definitions, per CONTRIBUTING.md; they have complete proofs.
The definitions live in the problem file (the task restricts output to a single file); a maintainer might prefer moving `IsSubnormal` to FormalConjecturesForMathlib as a reusable notion.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.74

by J. G. Thompson

A subnormal subgroup $H \lhd\lhd G$ of a group $G$ is said to be *good* if and only if
$\langle H, J \rangle \lhd\lhd G$ whenever $J \lhd\lhd G$. Is it true that when $H$ and $K$
are good subnormal subgroups of $G$, then $H \cap K$ is good?

Here $H \lhd\lhd G$ means that $H$ is subnormal in $G$: there is a finite chain of subgroups
$H = H_0 \lhd H_1 \lhd \dots \lhd H_n = G$, each normal in the next. The group $G$ is
arbitrary (possibly infinite). In a finite group the join of two subnormal subgroups is
always subnormal (Wielandt), so every subnormal subgroup of a finite group is good.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.74»

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]

/-- `IsNormalIn A B` means $A \lhd B$: the subgroup $A$ is contained in the subgroup $B$ and
is a normal subgroup of $B$. -/
def IsNormalIn (A B : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  A ≤ B ∧ (A.subgroupOf B).Normal

/-- A subgroup $H$ of $G$ is *subnormal*, written $H \lhd\lhd G$, if there is a finite chain
of subgroups $H = H_0 \lhd H_1 \lhd \dots \lhd H_n = G$ with each $H_i$ normal in $H_{i+1}$. -/
def IsSubnormal (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen IsNormalIn H ⊤

/-- A subnormal subgroup $H \lhd\lhd G$ is *good* if $\langle H, J \rangle \lhd\lhd G$
whenever $J \lhd\lhd G$. The join $\langle H, J \rangle$ is `H ⊔ J`. -/
def IsGood (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  IsSubnormal H ∧ ∀ J : Subgroup G, IsSubnormal J → IsSubnormal (H ⊔ J)

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isSubnormal_top : IsSubnormal (⊤ : Subgroup G) :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen.refl

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsSubnormal.of_normal (H : Subgroup G) [hH : H.Normal] : IsSubnormal H :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen.single ⟨le_top, hH.subgroupOf ⊤⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem isGood_top : IsGood (⊤ : Subgroup G) :=
  ⟨isSubnormal_top, fun J _ => by rw [top_sup_eq]; exact isSubnormal_top⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsGood.isSubnormal {H : Subgroup G} (hH : IsGood H) : IsSubnormal H :=
  hH.1

/--
A subnormal subgroup $H \lhd\lhd G$ of a group $G$ is said to be *good* if and only if
$\langle H, J \rangle \lhd\lhd G$ whenever $J \lhd\lhd G$. Is it true that when $H$ and $K$
are good subnormal subgroups of $G$, then $H \cap K$ is good?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.74» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (H K : Subgroup G), IsGood H → IsGood K → IsGood (H ⊓ K) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.74»

normal subgroup of $H_{i+1}$. -/
def IsSubnormal (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (c : Fin (n + 1) → Subgroup G), c 0 = H ∧ c (Fin.last n) = ⊤ ∧
    ∀ i : Fin n, c i.castSucc ≤ c i.succ ∧ ((c i.castSucc).subgroupOf (c i.succ)).Normal

theorem isSubnormal_of_normal {H : Subgroup G} (hH : H.Normal) : IsSubnormal H :=

    simpa [Subgroup.subgroupOf, Subgroup.comap] using hH.comap (⊤ : Subgroup G).subtype⟩

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsGood.isSubnormal {H : Subgroup G} (h : IsGood H) : IsSubnormal H :=
  h.1

/-- The whole group is a good subnormal subgroup of itself. -/

theorem isGood_top : IsGood (⊤ : Subgroup G) :=
  ⟨isSubnormal_top, fun _ _ => by simpa using isSubnormal_top⟩

$H$ to $G$ in which every subgroup is normal in the next one. -/
def IsSubnormal (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  Relation.ReflTransGen
    (fun H K : Subgroup G => H ≤ K ∧ (H.subgroupOf K).Normal) H ⊤

subnormal in $G$ for every subnormal subgroup $J$ of $G$. -/
def IsGood (H : Subgroup G) : Prop :=
  IsSubnormal H ∧ ∀ J : Subgroup G, IsSubnormal J → IsSubnormal (H ⊔ J)

then $H \cap K$ is good?
-/
